'And Jacob was cooking pottage, and Esau came from the field hungry; and he said to Jacob his brother: give me of this red pottage. And Jacob said to him: sell me thy birthright, and I will give thee bread, and also some of this pottage' — Jubilees preserves the Gen 25 transaction with the explicit verbal contract. Tewahedo Andǝmta exegesis frames this as the canonical case-study in the Tewahedo doctrine of consequential-choice (mərč'a-bä-yäwär̄əd, 'choosing-that-cuts-downward'): Esau's transaction is binding precisely because it was freely entered. The Tewahedo emphasizes against any 'irresistible-grace' framework that some choices truly close future possibilities — the birthright is not recoverable later (Heb 12:17, picked up by Tewahedo Pauline preaching), even though tears are sincere.

The Tewahedo diaspora theology (those who remain in Ethiopia during persecution vs. those who emigrate) finds its canonical discernment-pattern here: divine guidance, not circumstance, governs the legitimacy of staying-or-going.
